summary: Hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for NovaSearch. Walked through embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint flow, Console for ops/metrics, and Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization. Customer is interested in a short pilot to validate relevance improvements and cost/latency tradeoffs; security and data residency questions raised.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - Jordan from Redwood Inference here. We got Priya from the SE team and Samira on for handoff. How's everyone?
[00:06] Mark: Hey, Mark here. Good, excited to see what you have for embeddings + rerank, we're hoping to improve our top-k results for commerce use cases.
[00:12] Leah: Hi, Leah - want to understand engineering lift and SLA options.
[00:18] Priya: Great - quick agenda: quick intro, live demo of embeddings endpoint, show rerank endpoint flow, then Console + Optimize recommendations and next steps. We'll leave 10-12 min at the end for Q&A.
[00:29] Omar: Sounds good. We're mainly using Elastic + a small in-house embed pipeline today.
[00:34] Jordan: Cool. Quick qual - what's your current queries per second on search?
[00:39] Mark: For our primary product page it's about 120 qps peak and 40 steady. Latency target is sub 120 ms for end-to-end search, but we can tolerate a bit more for ML rerank if it's batchy.
[00:50] Priya: Good context. For the demo I'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint: simple REST call that returns a 1,024-d vector (model selection configurable), then a rerank endpoint that takes the original hits + embeddings and returns reranked result with scores.
[01:05] Priya: Opening my screen - first the API playground - here's a sample request to /v1/embeddings, payload with text, model: redwood-embed-large (demo). Response shows vector with float array - apologies transcription may flatten some punctuation.
[01:20] Priya: Now for rerank: POST /v1/rerank with inputs: query, candidate documents (id, text, metadata). The service computes embeddings on the fly or you can pass precomputed vectors. It then scores candidates and returns ranked ids + normalized scores.
[01:37] Jordan: We often recommend passing precomputed vectors for candidates to reduce cost; you only call embed for the query in real-time.
[01:44] Omar: Can you show an example where we precompute?
[01:47] Priya: Sure - switching to notebook. Here we show a small pipeline: bulk embed of corpus (batching), store vectors in vector DB (we demo with a local FAISS toy), query-time: embed query -> knn -> call rerank with top 50 candidates. The rerank endpoint applies cross-encoder style scoring and usually improves MRR.
[02:12] Mark: Do you have numbers on typical latency for rerank of 50 candidates?
[02:16] Priya: On hosted, typical P95 for rerank(50) is ~80-180 ms depending on model and whether query embedding is precomputed. For the demo infra it's about 120 ms. There are tradeoffs with model size and quantization.
[02:28] Leah: How does batching play into this - if we have bursts, will batching add extra waiting?
[02:33] Priya: Redwood has workload-aware batching; you can set latency SLOs and cost tiers. For low-latency routes we keep small batch windows; for throughput-focused routes we increase window to amortize cost. Console shows per-route latency distribution.
[02:46] Priya: Switching to Console - here's a per-route dashboard, token-level cost breakdown, and a rerank-specific trace that shows query embed -> kNN -> rerank call. You can set alerts on regression for relevance drop.
[03:02] Jordan: To address residency/security - we support Hosted with customer data controls, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC deployments with KMS. Tina, any specific certs?
[03:12] Tina: We need SOC2 type 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys for pilot. Also residency in us-east.
[03:23] Jordan: We have SOC2 and SAML SSO; we can share the security pack after the call and confirm KMS options for Private in-region deployments.
[03:31] Mark: Pricing - how do you bill for embeddings + rerank?
[03:35] Jordan: Hosted pricing is per-embedding unit and per-rerank call (or per-token for full model scoring). For precomputed candidate vectors we only bill query embed + rerank compute; we'll send a pricing sheet with example math for your QPS.
[03:47] Omar: For our scale, cost is a big driver - how much can you save with quantized models or Redwood Optimize?
[03:52] Priya: Optimize recommends quantization level and batching configs per model/route. In benchmarks we commonly see 2-3x cost reduction using int8 and smarter batching without meaningful relevance loss. We'll run a recommendation after we see your dataset.
[04:05] Leah: If we need to test relevance, what's the fastest POC we can run?
[04:09] Priya: Typical 1-week rerank pilot: you send 500-2k sample queries with labels, we run baseline vs Redwood rerank and share MRR/precision@k with cost/latency estimates. That's what we proposed as next step.
[04:20] Jordan: We'll pair you with a Solutions Engineer for the POC and share the eval harness + baseline template.
[04:26] Mark: Great. A couple of technical Qs - does rerank use cross-encoder or a hybrid? Is it re-ranking by concatenating query+doc?
[04:34] Priya: We use a configurable reranker; default is a light cross-encoder that concatenates query+doc for fine-grained scoring. For scale-critical flows we support a hybrid two-stage approach: dense retrieval -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank on top-k.
[04:47] Omar: How do we handle cold-start or docs with long context?
[04:51] Priya: For long docs we recommend chunking with overlap, store chunk vectors; rerank at chunk level then aggregate scores per document. Cold-start can be bootstrapped with heuristic rescoring or by using synthetic queries.
[05:05] Jordan: I'm going to demo a live rerank example - sending a query 'wireless earbuds warranty' and a set of 10 candidate docs.
[05:12] Priya: Posting request now - you can see the JSON request and response includes ranked ids and scores. A note on transcription: sometimes model names like 'redwood-embed-large' get mangled in the auto transcript.
[05:25] Leah: We saw a 12% lift in MRR in your demo - what's the baseline?
[05:29] Priya: Baseline was their candidate scoring using simple lexical features + BM25; rerank model added semantic relevance. Exact numbers depend on your labels, but the demo shows relative improvement.
[05:39] Tina: About data retention - for hosted, do you keep raw customer queries? Are they used for training?
[05:44] Jordan: Hosted has configurable data retention; by default we don't train customer data into public models and we have contractual clauses. For strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private with explicit KMS and no data usage for training. We'll include the security doc link.
[05:58] Mark: On integration, we use Golang + their own vector store. How heavy is SDK work?
[06:03] Priya: We provide REST API and official SDKs (Python, JS). For Golang you can use the REST endpoint directly; we can share example code. For vector DB compatibility we work with FAISS, Pinecone, Milvus, etc.
[06:16] Omar: What's the expected dev time for pilot integration?
[06:19] Jordan: For a simple hosted pilot - probably 1-2 engineer days to plug in sample queries and run evals. If you want private deployment it takes more time (onboarding infra), which we can scope after pilot.
[06:31] Priya: Quick note on model variants - you can pin model versions and use fallback policies. If a larger model is slow we can fallback to a smaller quantized variant.
[06:41] Leah: Any regulatory issues with EU users?
[06:44] Jordan: We have region options; for EU data residency we can propose private deployments in EU cloud regions. We'll confirm in the security pack.
[06:54] Mark: Ok wrapped up - what's immediate next step?
[06:57] Jordan: We'll send pricing and security pack. Priya will send demo notebook + rerank code. We want Omar to send sample queries; Tina to confirm security checklist points. We'll aim to start pilot on 2026-10-12.
[07:10] Jordan: Anything else?
[07:12] Leah: No, that's it. Thanks.
[07:14] Samira: Thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invite for kickoff.
[07:18] Mark: Thanks.
[07:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic speech recognition occasionally merged model names and product terms (e.g., "KV cache" -> "k v cash"), and speaker labels are accurate but there are small misalignments.
